defects: Restricted to the real field ℝ only, dropping the gold's general RCLike 𝕜 (so the ℂ case, covered by the gold, is lost)

Forces E and F to be finite-dimensional of the SAME dimension n (via requiring bases indexed by a common Fin n for both), which is a hypothesis not present in the gold: gold only assumes FiniteDimensional 𝕜 U, leaving V's dimension (and even finite-dimensionality) unconstrained, so gold's theorem is strictly more general

Formalizes 'norm-determinant' by universally quantifying over explicit orthonormal bases b_E, b_F and their orthonormality hypotheses and computing an ordinary square-matrix determinant, instead of applying the gold's basis-independent, already-defined `LinearMap.normDet`; this adds extra hypotheses/parameters (the bases and orthonormality proofs) not present in gold's clean application form
Drops the ambient type W present in gold's variable block (minor)

Conclusion is phrased as |det (toMatrix b_F b_E f)| = 1 rather than f.toLinearMap.normDet = 1, making it a differently-scoped (basis- and dimension-restricted) proposition rather than the same statement up to renaming/notation
